gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-newa: Eater has jagged, wide-spaced letters with short ascenders, and its thin strokes stay sturdy instead of turning brittle. Noto Sans Newa comes in behind it with a plain sans build, tall bowls and a clearly open e that does the quiet, steady reading.
gen-fs-bonny-outfit: Bonny sets tight lines of literary serif, with gaping curves and a light stroke contrast you only notice up close. But Outfit is built from one smooth, cable-like line with curves that stop short of closing, which makes it the friendlier voice.
gen-almendra-display-gf-radio-canada: Ornate and bookish, Almendra Display has a pronounced x-height and letters that refuse to pinch shut, so it flourishes when set big and brief. Radio Canada then takes over with a plain sans line of tall, full c, s and z that never changes pressure.
gen-audiowide-gf-radio-canada-big: Audiowide sets its glyphs like tiles with wide grout lines, every curve drawn without any thick-thin shift. And if the heading shrinks or Radio Canada Big grows large, that tile-like character fades while the sans body's tall, monoline shapes take over.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Aggressive and dark, Eater is jagged. Noto Sans Nushu has a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke, so a long run of it reads in an open, contemporary way that never feels cramped.
gen-fs-bonny-plus-jakarta-sans: Bonny is a refined literary serif whose thin strokes never turn spindly, set in tight lines with gaping curves. Plus Jakarta Sans follows with a precise monoline build and well-spaced curve endings, so the two sit together like a quiet old novel beside a modern timetable.
gen-almendra-display-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads in a steady weight from word to word, with broad terminal gaps and barely any stress in its curves. Almendra Display is the ornate one, best for a flourish up top, while Readex Pro does the sans work of carrying the text.
gen-audiowide-gf-roboto: Roboto reads clean and contemporary, with generous mouths on its round letters and capitals only slightly taller than the lowercase. Audiowide, drawn as if with a round-tipped pen, adds the futuristic edge, and the two settle into a page that feels both techy and approachable.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham reads clean, with wide gaps in the e. Eater is the dark, aggressive one, its strokes varying in weight only slightly, while the sans-serif body looks bold because its lowercase bodies are so tall.
gen-fs-bonny-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads neutral and geometric, each glyph a ribbon of constant width around counters that breathe. Bonny sets its literary serif above it, thin strokes not far from thick, and the two make a crisp, bookish pairing.
